data.content_ref: inline:The target's defense is self-defeating at the meta-level: it claims to avoid induction by re-framing preference as 'a strategic choice to employ the theory that has currently withstood the most rigorous attempts at refutation, thereby keeping the error-elimination process most active.' But any strategy presupposes that the chosen means will achieve the desired end in the future. The word 'thereby' in the target's own mechanism expresses a causal expectation — that employing currently-corroborated theories will keep error-elimination active going forward. This is an inductive inference about the future consequences of present strategic choices, grounded in the assumed persistence of the structural properties that make the strategy effective now. The target has not eliminated induction; it has displaced it from the object-level (the theory will remain true) to the meta-level (the methodological rule will keep error-elimination active). Since the claim asserts the defense is possible 'without smuggling induction,' and the strategic framing smuggles induction through the back door of expected strategic efficacy, the claim fails on its own terms — independently of the pragmatic-reliability objection already raised.
